title: सराय नाचको ऐतिहासिक तथा सांस्कृतिक महŒव
nepali: लेखसार दशैँको टीकापछि पूर्णिमा सम्म पहाडका टाकुरामा शक्तिपीठका रूपमा रहेका कोटमा सरायँ हुने प्रचलन रहेको छ । यो नाच लुम्बिनी प्रदेशका पहाडी जिल्लाहरू अर्घाखाँची, पाल्पा, गुल्मी र प्युठानमा विशेष रूपमा प्रचलित रहेको छ । पन्चेबाजा बजाएर हतियार सहित गरिने नृत्य, गीत र खेलको संयुक्तरूप सरायँ हो । सरायँ बसाइसराइका क्रममा तराई लगायतका स्थानमा विस्तार भएको छ । सरायँनाचको ऐतिहासिक तथा सांस्कृतिक महŒवको खोजी गर्न यो लेख तयार गरिएको हो । यस क्रममा सरायँहुने कोटहरूको स्थलगत अवलोकन, पूर्वकृतिहरूको अध्ययन, जानिफकारसँगको अन्तर्वार्ताका आधारमा तथ्य संकलन गरी वर्णनात्मकरूपमा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । यसको स्थलगत अवलोकन गुल्मी जिल्लाको इस्मा मैदान,अर्जै पोखराबारी, अमरपुर, सेउघा, मुसिकोट लगायतमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । सरायँनाचको ऐतिहासिकता प्राचीन मगरात संस्कृतिसँग जोडिदै चौबीसे राज्यकालबाट विशेष प्रचलनमा आएको पाइन्छ । सरायँ पहाडी जिल्लाबाट अन्यत्र विस्तार भए पनि यसको मौलिकता हराउँदै गएको छ । यो संस्कृति लोपोन्मुख हुन थालेको संकेत देखिएका छन् । यस नाचले मनोरञ्जन मात्र हैन सामाजिक एकता र मेलमिलाप बढाउन योगदान पुराएको छ । यो नाचले हाम्रो ऐतिहासिक मूल्यलाई बोकेको छ । शक्तिको उपासना, हतियार तथा औजारहरूको प्रदर्शनले विगत राज्यहरू बीचको लडाइ, विजयोत्सव, युद्धको तयारीको प्रतिबिम्बन सरायँमा हुने गरेको पाइन्छ । यस नाचले सामाजिक एकता र सहकार्यको सन्देश दिएको छ । यसले परम्परागत मूल्यमान्यता र पुर्खाको गौरवलाई उजागर गरेको छ । समय क्रममा सरायँ नाच विस्तार भएको भए पनि मौलिकता गुमाउँदै गएको, नयाँ पुस्तामा कम हस्तान्तरण भएकोले लोपोन्मुख हुने संभावना रहेको देखिएको छ । यसकारण यस अमूर्त सम्पदाको संरक्षणका लागि व्यवस्थित योजना बनाइ मौलिकता सहितको सरायँ नाच हुने स्थिति सिर्जना गर्नुपर्छ ।
american_english: Abstract: From Dashain Tika until the full moon, there is a tradition of holding Saraya at kots situated as shakti peethas atop mountain peaks. This dance is especially prevalent in the hill districts of Lumbini Province: Arghakhanchi, Palpa, Gulmi, and Pyuthan. Saraya is a combined form of dance, song, and martial play performed with weapons while playing the Panche Baja. In the course of migration, Saraya has expanded to locations including the Terai. This article was prepared to explore the historical and cultural significance of the Saraya dance. In this process, facts were collected and presented descriptively based on field observation of the kots where Saraya is held, the study of previous works, and interviews with key informants. Its field observation was focused on Isma Maidan, Arjai Pokharabari, Amarpur, Seugha, Musikot, and other locations in Gulmi district. Connecting with ancient Magarat culture, the historicity of the Saraya dance is found to have come into prominent practice during the Chaubise Rajya period. Even though Saraya has spread from the hill districts to other regions, its originality has been waning. Signs have emerged that this culture is beginning to become endangered. This dance has contributed not only to entertainment, but also to promoting social unity and reconciliation. This dance carries our historical values. Through the worship of Shakti and the display of weapons and implements, past battles between kingdoms, victory celebrations, and preparations for war are found to be reflected in Saraya. This dance has conveyed a message of social unity and cooperation. It has highlighted traditional values and ancestral pride. Although the Saraya dance has expanded over the course of time, it appears at risk of disappearing because it has been losing its originality and has been passed down less to the younger generation. Therefore, a systematic plan must be formulated to preserve this intangible heritage and create conditions for the Saraya dance to be held with its authenticity intact.

informal_english: Abstract: From Dashain Tika right through to the full moon, there's a tradition of putting on Saraya up at kots that serve as shakti peethas on mountain peaks. This dance is especially popular around the hill districts of Lumbini Province: Arghakhanchi, Palpa, Gulmi, and Pyuthan. Saraya is basically a mix of dancing, singing, and weapon play done while cranking out the Panche Baja. As folks migrated, Saraya spread out to other spots including the Terai. This paper was put together to dig into the historical and cultural significance of the Saraya dance. In this process, facts were gathered and laid out descriptively from field visits to the kots where Saraya happens, checking out past works, and having a yarn with people in the know. The fieldwork focused on spots in Gulmi district like Isma Maidan, Arjai Pokharabari, Amarpur, Seugha, Musikot, and the like. Tying back to ancient Magarat culture, the Saraya dance really seems to have taken off during the Chaubise kingdom period. Even though Saraya has spread out from the hill districts, it's been losing its authentic touch. There are signs this culture is starting to face extinction, mate. This dance hasn't just offered entertainment, but has also done heaps to build social unity and community harmony. This dance carries our historical values, no worries. Through worshipping Shakti and displaying weapons and tools, old-time battles between kingdoms, victory bashes, and preparations for war are reflected in Saraya. This dance sends out a solid message of social unity and cooperation. It really highlights traditional values and ancestral pride. Even though the Saraya dance has spread over time, it's in danger of dying out because it's lost its original flavour and hasn't been handed down much to the younger mob. So, we need to sort out a proper plan to preserve this intangible heritage and make sure the Saraya dance can keep going with its true spirit intact.
